questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: calculate water hardness from an EDTA titration
questions.stem: Sample 1601: A 52.08251478616148 mL water sample requires 23.80 mL of 0.0307 M EDTA. Express the hardness as mg/L as CaCO3 (molar mass 100.09 g/mol).

options.misconception: mixes the volume and molar-mass terms incorrectly
inverts the ratio of titrant to sample volume
forgets to convert grams to milligrams

questions.explanation: EDTA complexes metal ions one to one, so moles of EDTA equal moles of hardness expressed as calcium carbonate. Multiplying by the molar mass and one thousand gives milligrams, and dividing by the sample volume in liters gives the hardness in mg/L.
questions.hint: Moles EDTA times 100.09 g/mol, then convert to mg/L.
